input.question: What rights have we as Americans lost since 9/11?
input.ground_truth: Among others: * Rights to privacy - There is extensive monitoring of communications, including email and phones. It's hard to know exactly what is being monitored because it's a secret. * Rights to due process - More than one American citizen has been either held in prison (Jose Padilla) or executed (Anwar al-Aulaqi) without a trial, because there was a charge against them. They couldn't fight these charges because the charges themselves were state secrets that couldn't be revealed by the prosecutors. * Rights to freedom of speech - More than one US citizen has been put in jail because they were charged with supporting terrorists in indirect ways. In at least one case the person was charged with supporting terrorism because he made a YouTube video. I'll write more if I get a minute, but these are just a few examples from the past 12 years of changes to US domestic policies.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

response.prediction: Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of toys that your parents say you can play with. On a special day (called 9/11), something really sad happened, and after that, your parents made some new rules about your toys. Now, you can’t play with some of your toys the same way as before. For example, you can’t bring certain toys to school, or sometimes grown-ups have to check your toys to make sure they’re safe. Also, sometimes grown-ups can’t talk about some things they want to, or they have to show papers to travel. These are like some of the toys you can’t play with the same way anymore. These are called "rights," and after 9/11, some of them got a little harder to use. But lots of toys (rights) are still there for you!
